Let  
\[
Q_k=\prod_{i=1}^k\left(1-\frac1{P_i}\right).
\]
Then
\[
Q_k-Q_{k+1}=Q_k\left(1-\left(1-\frac1{P_{k+1}}\right)\right)=\frac{Q_k}{P_{k+1}}.
\]
Also,
\[
\prod_{i=1}^k \frac{P_i-1}{P_{i+1}}
=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^k(P_i-1)}{\prod_{i=2}^{k+1}P_i}
=\frac{P_1}{P_{k+1}}\prod_{i=1}^k\frac{P_i-1}{P_i}
=\frac{2}{P_{k+1}}Q_k.
\]
Thus each term equals
\[
2(Q_k-Q_{k+1}).
\]
So the sum telescopes:
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2(Q_k-Q_{k+1})
=2Q_1-2\lim_{n\to\infty}Q_n.
\]
Since \(Q_1=1-\frac12=\frac12\), and
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}Q_n=\prod_p\left(1-\frac1p\right)=0
\]
because \(\sum_p \frac1p\) diverges, the sum is
\[
2\cdot \frac12=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
